candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central venous access infection prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC-recommended aseptic central venous catheter access practices in outpatient oncology, including hand hygiene and antiseptic disinfection of the needleless connector before access.

options.A: Perform hand hygiene, use aseptic technique with clean gloves, scrub the injection cap with an appropriate antiseptic, and allow it to dry before access.
options.B: Skip disinfection of the injection cap if it appears visibly clean and the catheter was used earlier the same day.
options.C: Touch the disinfected injection cap to confirm that it is dry before connecting the sterile syringe or IV tubing.
options.D: Use maximal sterile barrier precautions for every routine catheter access because they are required for ongoing central-line maintenance.

candidate.rationale: CDC's outpatient oncology infection-control plan directs healthcare personnel accessing PICCs and tunneled central venous catheters to maintain aseptic technique, perform hand hygiene, wear clean gloves, scrub the injection cap or needleless connector with an appropriate antiseptic, allow it to dry, and then access it with the syringe or IV tubing. Routine access should not bypass cap disinfection. Maximal sterile barrier precautions are associated with central-line insertion, not every routine access procedure.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For PICC and tunneled central venous catheter access in outpatient oncology, CDC directs personnel to maintain aseptic technique, perform hand hygiene, wear clean gloves, scrub the injection cap with an appropriate antiseptic and allow it to dry, then access the cap with a syringe or IV tubing.
